chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated to us from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Kufi, from Abdullah al-Dahqan, from Durust, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Behold, is it possible that a man will lie about me while he is reclining on his haunches? They said: O Messenger of Allah, and who is the one who will lie about you? He said: The one to whom the narration reaches and he says: 'This was not said by the Messenger of Allah.' So, whatever narration comes to you from me that agrees with the truth, I said it; and whatever narration comes to you from me that does not agree with the truth, I did not say it, and I will not say except the truth.
ai.seo_question: How does the Prophet distinguish authentic hadith from fabricated ones based on their conformity to truth?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Mani al-Akhbar*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) addresses the critical issue of *al-kadhib* (the liar) who dismisses authentic traditions merely by asserting 'I did not hear this,' thereby highlighting the tension between oral transmission and textual authority. He establishes a pragmatic criterion for verification: any report aligning with the truth (*al-haqq*) is accepted as his, reinforcing the Shia principle that the Prophet’s speech is inherently truthful and consistent with divine reality. This hadith underscores the importance of evaluating narrations based on their substantive truthfulness rather than solely on chain of transmission, a key theme in Usul al-Hadith.
